statement: Centre-free profinite extensions are the pullback of Aut(Delta) over Out(Delta); sections correspond to effective lifts modulo geometric inner conjugacy.
notes: No faithfulness of E→Aut(Delta) by itself is asserted.

statement: The literal maximal-closed-subgroup open-normalizer characterization of cuspidal inertia is false, already for the rational tripod.
manuscript_passages: §34, scan483, folio245, main text and margin
notes: Complete curve-group counterexample Delta itself; proper characteristic commutator counterexample; rational point sections distinguish arithmetic decomposition groups. Computation in code/d_counterexamples.py.

statement: For affine hyperbolic curves over number fields, the full cyclotomic normalizer condition recognizes nontrivial inertia elements and maximal peripheral procyclic subgroups.
notes: The extra cyclotomic character condition is essential to the cited theorem. Full profinite groups; no statement for arbitrary bare invariant loop structures.

statement: Relative open Hom over a sub-p-adic field is equivalent to dominant morphisms of hyperbolic curves, modulo geometric inner conjugacy; inertia is killed or maps into peripheral inertia.
depends_on: Mochizuki1999, Theorem A = Theorem16.5 and following Remark
notes: All primes p, including2,3. Proper and affine. The geometrically pro-p version keeps the full arithmetic quotient.

statement: Effective lifts transported from pointed hyperbolic curves through equivariant outer isomorphisms are exactly rational-point sections.
notes: Geometrically admissible is defined precisely; it does not include every abstract splitting.

statement: Not all sections of an affine hyperbolic curve over a number field arise from its interior rational points.
notes: Complete rational tangential section at0 of the tripod; Kummer calculation rules out every interior rational point.

statement: 019 claims the proper p-adic section conjecture via the specified-embedding completion theorem; that new completion theorem is unverified in this audit.
notes: Open; claimed. Entire main preprint read. No counterexample or fatal gap is asserted; uniform stable-coordinate and all-sheet analytic construction not independently established. Companion not used as a verified proof. No Lean dependency.

statement: Assuming 019 Theorem1.2 in its specified embedding, its completion argument rigorously implies the proper local section theorem.
notes: Proved conditional implication, not unconditional certification of019. Includes residue characteristic2 via quantitative Hensel inequality.

statement: Assuming proper local section surjectivity at finite places, localized global sections equal the finite-cover descent set; global section surjectivity is equivalent to that set being the rational diagonal.
notes: Modified adeles use real components and omit complex factors. This is an equivalence, not a proof that all finite-descent sets equal rational points.

statement: Conditionally on the local section theorem, every section of Y_1(N)/Q with genus X_1(N)≥2 compactifies to the section of a unique rational cusp; this is the consequence for modular sections.
notes: It does not prove that the affine section itself is cuspidal and does not imply nonexistence of moduli sections. Tangential cusp sections exist.

statement: Every continuous open homomorphism between full arithmetic groups of hyperbolic curves over number fields sends the source geometric kernel into the target geometric kernel.
notes: Unconditional. The image is tfg closed normal in an open absolute Galois subgroup. This missing argument is supplied before invoking031.

statement: Assuming031 for absolute Galois groups, absolute open Hom classes are dominant curve morphisms over uniquely reconstructed embeddings of number fields.
notes: Proved conditional reduction. Known cases: injective quotient map, isomorphisms, cyclotomic compatible quotient map, and source fieldQ. Arithmetic versus geometric inner ambiguity is stated.

statement: 031 claims the unrestricted open-Hom theorem for global solvably closed Galois groups; the uniform arithmetic separation step remains unverified in this audit.
notes: Open; claimed. All new lemma proofs read and used external primary statements checked. No counterexample or fatal error asserted. Lemma3.1/Proposition4.3/Proposition5.3 generality not independently established.

statement: Nonabelian geometric profinite free and hyperbolic surface groups are torsion-free and slim; number-field absolute Galois groups are slim and have no nontrivial finite normal subgroup.
notes: Galois groups may contain complex conjugations: centre-free does not mean torsion-free. Low nonhyperbolic types excluded.

statement: For these geometric groups an automorphism fixing an open subgroup is identity; centralizers of nonzero powers of the specified simple generators equal their procyclic closures.
notes: Both genus-zero generators and standard proper-surface generators treated. Endomorphism reading in the rank-one intermediate calculation suffices; notation uncertainty does not affect conclusion.

statement: The full profinite outer Galois action of every hyperbolic curve over a number field or p-adic local field is faithful.
notes: Affine and proper distinguished; complete Belyi tripod deduction supplied. A single-prime geometric quotient is not faithful over number fields.

statement: For every hyperbolic moduli type the arithmetic outer-image quotient by orientation-preserving geometric monodromy is G_Q; total monodromy injectivity is equivalent to geometric injectivity.
notes: Ordered and unordered variants treated using finite-index descent. No congruence conjecture assumed for quotient faithfulness. Does not compute the full normalizer quotient.

statement: Faithful outer action passes from a hyperbolic base curve to every geometrically connected finite étale cover over the same characteristic-zero field.
notes: Direction and unchanged base field proved directly; no rational point is needed.

statement: The centralizer of the rational tripod Galois action in Out(Fhat2) is its automorphism group S3.
notes: Sub-p-adic base fields; complete deduction from relative Isom. S3 font ambiguity has no mathematical effect.

statement: Hyperbolicity cannot be dropped from a uniform faithfulness theorem: types(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0) admit counterexamples.
notes: Complete CM elliptic counterexample overQ(i), with S3 quotient and explicit commuting adelic centralizer. Finite computations included. Hyperbolic types(0,3),(1,1) distinguished by peripheral structure.

statement: Orientation-preserving geometric monodromy is essential to the quotient-faithfulness theorem; an extended mapping-class quotient kills complex conjugation. Real, nonorientable, and small-prime scopes differ explicitly.
notes: Geometric centres remain trivial overR; G_R=C2 is not slim. Real sections classify components. Nonorientable quotients are not geometric complex-curve surface groups. p=2,3 retained for all stated characteristic-zero arithmetic theorems.

statement: A Galois-invariant alternative tripod loop structure is necessarily the usual peripheral system.
notes: A complete proof obtains cyclotomic exponents from primitive abelianizations and then applies inertia recognition; this argument does not cover the once-punctured elliptic commutator.

statement: The bare invariant-loop uniqueness assertion in other affine types and the proposed admissible moduli splitting characterization are unresolved by the audit in their stated generality.
notes: Open means not established in this audit, not a claim that no theorem exists in the literature. Smallest remaining loop type(1,1); identify missing cyclotomic exponent condition. No global proper SC is inferred.
